D010-D005_h001.question:

I’ve been driving extra hours, and when I get paid, I blow the money on stupid stuff—expensive gadgets, clothes I don’t need. My bank account is a mess, and my ex is furious because I’m behind on support.

Lately I feel like random things are aimed at me—the songs on the radio, people talking on the street—I’m convinced they’re about me. I also sometimes feel things crawling on my skin, like bugs, but there’s nothing there. That only started with this “amped up” period.

Before this, for about five months, I was the opposite—completely flat. I didn’t enjoy anything, not even seeing my kids. I’d stare at the wardrobe for ages, unable to decide what to wear, or sit at a diner and not manage to pick from the menu. It felt like I was empty inside, and it got so bad I could barely work.

D010-D005_h021.question:
I started having these “up” periods about two weeks ago. At first I felt amazing, like I had endless energy. At the station I’d clean all the pumps, rearrange the shelves, try to talk to every customer, and then on my breaks I’d start three or four different projects on my phone at once—looking up business ideas, texting everybody, making playlists. But I can’t stick with anything for more than a few minutes; my mind just jumps. I’ll go from laughing and feeling on top of the world to snapping at coworkers if they move too slow or question me.

During these highs I’ve been hearing voices, like a couple of guys talking behind me, commenting on what I’m doing or saying my girlfriend is cheating on me. We’re not even that serious, but I get this fixed idea she’s with someone else, checking her socials over and over, even though there’s nothing there. Those voices and suspicions only happen when I’m in this revved‑up state.

Before this, for about two months, I was the opposite—barely talking, moving slow, no drive to work, just wishing I wouldn’t wake up, but not planning anything.
D010-D005_h021.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D010-D005_h021.answer: B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D005_h022.question:
It’s like I’ve been living two different lives this year.

About three months ago I had this stretch, maybe two weeks, where I felt incredible. I was barely sleeping, three hours a night, and still buzzing with energy. I’d be pacing around my condo at 3 a.m., reorganizing closets, planning to double my listings, texting clients nonstop. I couldn’t sit still in an open house; I’d flit from room to room, starting conversations I didn’t finish because my mind kept jumping. I couldn’t focus on paperwork for more than a minute before jumping to another idea.

During that time I started feeling like the world was sending me messages. A random billboard would feel like it was talking directly to me about a property, or a news anchor seemed to be hinting at my life. I also kept seeing people out of the corner of my eye—figures in doorways or sitting at an empty table at a showing—but when I looked straight at them, no one was there. Those things only happened during that “high” period.

Since then it’s crashed. For the last two months, I feel nothing—no joy from closing a sale, no interest in my kids’ texts. Even walking from my car to a house feels like wading through mud; I move slowly, drag my feet, just stare. I’ve stopped following up with clients; my listings are slipping. Sometimes, driving between showings, I get these sudden urges to just swerve into traffic or step off a parking garage, not with a plan, more like a pull. It scares me, but I also feel too numb and slowed down to care much.
D010-D005_h022.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D010-D005_h022.answer: B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D005_h023.question:
It’s kind of hard to put into words, because it’s like I’ve been two completely different people this past year.

About three months ago, I had this two‑week stretch where I felt incredible, like I was on top of the world. I barely slept and didn’t feel tired. At work I was buzzing around the depot nonstop, rearranging routes, jumping from one task to another and never finishing anything. I couldn’t sit still, even at home. My mind was racing so much I couldn’t stick with a single thought or conversation; I’d start talking about one thing and jump to another before my wife could respond.

During that time I became convinced this woman in the council office was secretly in love with me because of how she said hello once. I was sure of it. I also kept smelling this sweet, almost floral scent, like perfume or air freshener, even when I was alone in the yard and no one else noticed it. Those smells and beliefs only happened during that “high” period.

Since then, for the last two months, it’s flipped completely. I don’t enjoy anything—family, football, nothing. I move and talk slowly; my wife has to repeat questions because it takes me a while to answer. I go to work but I’m just going through the motions. Most nights I lie in bed thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up, though I haven’t made any plans to hurt myself.
D010-D005_h023.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D010-D005_h023.answer: B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D005_h024.question:
For the last couple of years I feel like I’ve been swinging between two different people.

About three months ago I hit a real low that’s still kind of dragging on. I stopped caring about pretty much everything, even the animals. Normally I love being in with the giraffes and the big cats, but lately it’s like I’m just…empty. I go through the motions, but there’s no pleasure in it, not even with my kids at home. I pace the enclosure paths on my breaks, wringing my hands or picking at my fingers, because I can’t sit still even though I feel exhausted. Most days I catch myself thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up, or that everyone would be better off without me, but I haven’t planned anything.

Right before this, there was a two‑week stretch where I was the opposite. I barely slept, had endless energy, and was bouncing from enclosure repairs to new enrichment projects to reorganizing feed schedules without finishing anything. My mood flipped on a dime—one minute joking with coworkers, the next snapping at them. I was sure the zoo announcements and even the way the lions roared were secret messages about me. I heard voices in the empty corridors calling my name and commenting on my work. Those voices and ideas stopped once that “high” ended and the crash into this long low began.
D010-D005_h024.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D010-D005_h024.answer: B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D005_h025.question:
It kind of feels like my life’s been split into two extremes this past year.

A couple months ago I had this stretch, about two weeks, where I barely slept and I was all over the place. In the kitchen at school I’d start three different dishes at once, then suddenly decide I needed to reorganize my whole station, then jump to planning a pop-up restaurant on my phone in the middle of class. I was moving nonstop, talking fast, snapping at people if they interrupted me—even something tiny, like a classmate asking to borrow a whisk, made me furious. I got so worked up I couldn’t finish anything and ended up getting kicked out of lab for being disruptive. Around that time I became convinced something terrible was about to happen to the world, like everything was going to collapse soon. Sometimes I’d feel things crawling on my skin or like someone brushed past me when no one was there. Those weird sensations and beliefs only happened during that “amped up” period.

Now it’s the opposite. For the past two months I’ve been dragging myself around, moving and talking slowly, skipping classes. Cooking used to be my favorite thing; now even tasting food feels pointless. I don’t feel happy or close to anyone. I catch myself thinking about just stepping into traffic or off a balcony—not with a plan, more like an urge to end this numb, heavy feeling.
D010-D005_h025.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D010-D005_h025.answer: B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
